<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="ShakespeareFan00" /></noinclude><section begin="par95" />''witness'' (from {{GHGheb|text=מוּת}}, {{GHGheb|text=עוּד}}), have likewise an unchangeable vowel in the first syllable. Cf., on the other hand, the forms from {{GHGheb|text=פ״י}} stems mentioned above, under e, such as {{GHGheb|text=שֵׁנָה|translate=sleep}}, constr. st. {{GHGheb|text=שְׁנַת}}; moreover, {{GHGheb|text=חֵמָה|translate=anger}}, constr. st. {{GHGheb|text=חֲמַת}} (but {{GHGheb|text=חֵ֫מֶת|translate=a leathern bottle}}, in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=חֶ֑מֶת}} [so Baer, Ginsb., but Kittel {{GHGheb|text=חֵ׳}}] {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=21|verse=15}}, ''constr. st.'' {{GHGheb|text=חֵ֫מַת מַ֫יִם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=21|verse=14}}, perhaps from a stem {{GHGheb|text=חמת}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|95|m}}
The feminines of the form ''qăṭŭl'', like {{GHGheb|text=עֲמֻקָּה}} (masc. {{GHGheb|text=עָמֹק}}), maintain the original ''ŭ'' by sharpening the following consonant (cf. {{GHGpar|93|kk}}); on the other hand, by appending the fem. {{GHGheb|text=ת}}, segholate forms arise like {{GHGheb|text=נְחֹ֫שֶׁת}}, before suff. {{GHGheb|text=נְחֻשְׁתָּם}}, &c. Dual {{GHGheb|text=נְחֻשְׁתַּ֫יִם}} (see Paradigm II ''a''); but cf. {{GHGheb|text=נְחָשְׁתִּי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=3|verse=7}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|95|n}}
A few (aramaising) feminines from {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}} stems (Paradigm II, ''c'') are found with the ending ''âth'', due to the rejection of the final {{GHGterm|Wāw}} or {{GHGterm|Yôdh}} and contraction of the preceding ''ă'' with the ''ă'' of the termination ''ăth''; thus {{GHGheb|text=מְנָת|translate=portion}} (for ''mănăyăth'' or ''mănăwăth''), {{GHGheb|text=קְצָת}} end (also {{GHGheb|text=קָצֶה}} and {{GHGheb|text=קָצָה}}), plur. {{GHGheb|text=מְנָיוֹת}} (''constr. st.'' {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=12|verse=47}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=13|verse=10|hidebook=1}}) and {{GHGheb|text=מְנָאוֹת}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=12|verse=44}}); {{GHGheb|text=קְצָוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=38|verse=5}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=37|verse=8|hidebook=1}} and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=39|verse=4|hidebook=1}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}}; on {{GHGheb|text=גֵּֽאָיֹת|translate=valleys}}, see {{GHGpar|93|v}}.—{{GHGheb|text=אוֹת|translate=sign}} (stem {{GHGheb|text=אוה}}) is obscured from {{GHGheb|text=אָת}}, and this is contracted from ''ʾâyăth'' = ''ʾăwăyăth''; plur. {{GHGheb|text=אֹתוֹת}}, with the double feminine ending; cf. above, f, and {{GHGpar|87|k}}.—The retention of the ''ā'' in the first syllable in {{GHGheb|text=אָֽלָתִי}}, &c., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=41}}, &c., is abnormal.

{{GHGmargin-letter|95|o}}
3. Paradigm III, cf. the various forms in {{GHGpar|94|d}} and f–h. The ''dual'' {{GHGheb|text=חֽוֹמֹתַ֫יִם|translate=two walls}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=22|verse=11}}, &c., taken directly from the plur. {{GHGheb|text=חוֹמוֹת}}, for {{GHGheb|text=חֽוֹמָתַ֫יִם}}, is abnormal (cf. {{GHGpar|87|s}}, and the proper name {{GHGheb|text=גְּדֵֽרֹתַיִם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=15|verse=36}}).—Among the forms resembling participles {{GHGterm|Qal}} of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}, such as {{GHGheb|text=זָרָה}} (masc. {{GHGheb|text=זָר}} from ''zâĭr'', hence with unchangeable ''â''), must be reckoned also {{GHGheb|text=בָּמָה|translate=high place}} (from {{GHGheb|text=בּוּם}}), which has for its ''constr. st. plur.'' the pleonastic form {{GHGheb|text=בָּֽמוֹתֵי}}, or written defectively {{GHGheb|text=בָּֽמֹתֵי}} (see {{GHGpar|87|s}}); for this the Masora everywhere requires {{GHGheb|text=בָּֽמֳתֵי}}, which is to be read ''bām<sup>o</sup>thê'' (not ''bŏm<sup>o</sup>thê''), with an anomalous shortening of the ''ô'' to {{GHGheb|text=־ֳ}}; but with suffixes {{GHGheb|text=בָּֽמוֹתַי}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|95|p}}
In a wider sense the feminines of the form {{GHGheb|text=קַטָּל}} ({{GHGpar|84|e|b}}) belong to this class, in so far as they shorten the ''â'' of the second syllable before the termination {{GHGheb|text=ת}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=דַּלֶּ֫קֶת|translate=inflammation}} (from ''dallăqt''), with suff. {{GHGheb|text=צַדֶּקְתֵּךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=52}}; {{GHGheb|text=טַבַּ֫עַת|translate=signet}}; also fem. of the forms {{GHGheb|text=קִטַּל}} and {{GHGheb|text=קִטֵּל}} ({{GHGpar|84|c|b}} and d), as {{GHGheb|text=אִוֶּ֫לֶת|translate=folly}} (for ''ʾiwwălt''), and of all the forms which have a changeable vowel in the second syllable, and are formed with the prefix {{GHGheb|text=מ‍}} ({{GHGpar|85|g}}–k), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=מַמְלָכָה|translate=kingdom}}, {{GHGterm|constr.}} always {{GHGheb|text=מַמְלֶ֫כֶת}}; {{GHGheb|text=מַזְמֵרָה}} (not used in the sing.) ''pruning-hook'', plur. {{GHGheb|text=מַזְמֵרוֹת}}; {{GHGheb|text=מַשְׂכֹּ֫רֶת}} ''reward'', with suff. {{GHGheb|text=מַשְׂכֻּרְתִּי}}; cf. also the examples given in {{GHGpar|85|g}} and p, like {{GHGheb|text=מוֹלֶ֫דֶת|translate=birth}} (but from {{GHGheb|text=ל״א}}, {{GHGheb|text=מֽוֹצָאָה|translate=outgoing}}), {{GHGheb|text=תּוֹלֶ֫דֶת|translate=generation}}, {{GHGheb|text=תּֽוֹעֵבָה|translate=abomination}}, constr. {{GHGheb|text=תּֽוֹעֲבַת}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|95|q}}
Sometimes the plural of these forms is to be traced to a secondary form, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אִגֶּ֫רֶת|translate=a letter}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=אִגְּרוֹת}} (as if from {{GHGheb|text=אִגְּרָה}}); also {{GHGheb|text=יֽוֹנְקוֹת}}, which is merely formed on the analogy of the other plur. fem. of participles {{GHGterm|Qal}}, is to be referred to a sing. {{GHGheb|text=יוֹנְקָה}}. Cf., moreover, {{GHGheb|text=מַֽחֲרֶ֫שֶׁת|translate=ploughshare}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=מַֽחֲרֵשׁוֹת}} (as if from {{GHGheb|text=מַֽחֲרֵשָׁה}})<ref>{{GHGheb|text=עַשְׁתֹּ֫רֶת|translate=Astarte}} (plur. {{GHGheb|text=עַשְׁתָּרוֹת}}), which was formerly included among these examples, is most probably due to an intentional alteration of the original {{GHGheb|text=עַשְׁתֶּ֫רֶת}}, like {{GHGheb|text=מֹ֫לֶךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=18|verse=21}}, &c. (for {{GHGheb|text=מֶ֫לֶךְ}}), with the vowels of {{GHGheb|text=בּ֫שֶׁת}} shame, the latter word being substituted in reading for the name of the goddess.</ref>; on the other hand, {{GHGheb|text=כֹּֽתָרוֹת|translate=capitals}} (of columns), and {{GHGheb|text=תּֽוֹכָחוֹת|translate=reproofs}}, are the regular plurals of {{GHGheb|text=כֹּתֶ֫רֶת}} and {{GHGheb|text=תּוֹכַ֫חַת}}.
<section end="par95" /><noinclude>
